title: components
text: Plain tags need no helper: Button, A, Input, Select, Textarea, Table, Dialog, Details, Progress, Meter and the headings are styled as they are. A Div has no look of its own; give it a class (card, row, hstack, vstack, container) or use the functions below. An accordion is plain Details(Summary('Title'), P('Body')).

title: fhoat
text:
fhoat adds the Oat CSS library to a FastHTML app. It replaces Pico, which FastHTML uses by default. Install fhoat, then pass oat=True to fast_app.
from fhoat import * imports everything in fasthtml.common and the fhoat components.

title: fhoat
text:
Examples

A page

nav = Navbar('My app', ('Docs', '#'), ('Blog', '#'), end=(ThemePicker(), ModeToggle()))
hero = Hero('Plan your week', eyebrow='My app',
            sub='Add your tasks and share them with your team.',
            actions=(ABtn('Sign up', href='#'), ABtn('Learn more', href='#', look='outline')))




A navbar and a hero




Buttons

buttons = Div(Btn('Primary'), Btn('Secondary', variant='secondary'), Btn('Danger', variant='danger'),
              Btn('Outline', look='outline'), Btn('Ghost', look='ghost'), Btn('Small', size='small'),
              ABtn('A link', href='#', look='outline'), Btn('Busy', aria_busy='true', disabled=True),
              cls='hstack mb-4')
group = ButtonGroup(*[Btn(o, look='outline') for o in ('Day', 'Week', 'Month')])




Buttons




Badges, avatars and alerts

badges = Div(Badge('New'), Badge('Draft', variant='secondary'), Badge('Live', variant='success'),
             Badge('Beta', variant='warning'), Badge('Down', variant='danger'),
             Avatar(initials='KR'), Avatar(initials='AB', size='large'), Spinner(size='sm'),
             cls='hstack mb-4')
alerts = Grid(Alert('Your changes are saved.', title='Saved', variant='success'),
              Alert('The disk is 90% full.', title='Warning', variant='warning'),
              Alert('The payment failed.', title='Error', variant='danger'))




Badges, avatars and alerts




Forms

signup = Card(Form(Field('Email', Input(type='email', name='email', placeholder='you@example.com'),
                         hint='We never share it.'),
                   Field('Plan', Select(Option('Free'), Option('Pro'), name='plan')),
                   Div(Switch('Email me updates', name='news', checked=True),
                       Label(Input(type='checkbox', name='tos'), 'I agree'), cls='hstack')),
              header=H3('Sign up'), footer=Btn('Join'))
checks = Card(Field('Email', Input(name='bad', value='name@'), error='Enter a valid email address.', invalid=True),
              Group(Input(type='search', name='q', placeholder='Search'), Btn('Go')),
              Input(type='range'), Progress(value=60, max=100),
              header=H3('Errors and HTML inputs'))




Forms




Tabs and tables

rows = [('Rigveda', '10,552', 'success', 'Live'), ('Tirukkuṟaḷ', '1,330', 'warning', 'Review'),
        ('Arthaśāstra', '5,348', 'secondary', 'Draft')]
works = Div(Table(Thead(Tr(Th('Work'), Th('Verses'), Th('State'))),
                  Tbody(*[Tr(Td(Strong(w)), Td(n), Td(Badge(b, variant=v))) for w, n, v, b in rows])),
            cls='table')

Tabs holding a table

swatch = lambda t: Card(Strong(t), Div(Btn('Save', size='small'), Badge('New'), cls='hstack mt-2'), data_theme=t)

The presets in light mode




Theme presets in dark mode

dark = Div(swatches, style='color-scheme:dark; background:var(--background); color:var(--foreground); padding:1rem')




The presets in dark mode




With htmx
This sign-up form sends the email to /join. If the email is not valid, the server sends back the form with an error. Otherwise, the server sends a toast.
def signup_form(email='', error=None):
    return Form(Field('Email', Input(name='email', type='email', value=email), error=error, invalid=bool(error)),
                Btn('Join'), hx_post='/join', hx_swap='outerHTML')

@rt
def join(email: str):
    if '@' not in email: return signup_form(email, 'Enter a valid email address.')
    return P('Thank you.'), toast_hdr('You signed up.', 'Welcome', 'success')
The button opens the dialog that has the same id.
DialogOpen('Delete', id='del'), DialogX(P('This cannot be undone.'), header=H3('Delete project?'),
                                        footer=(DialogClose('Cancel'), Btn('Delete', variant='danger', hx_delete='/p/1')),
                                        id='del')

OatBusy()

title: fhoat
text:
Plain tags
Oat styles Button, A, Input, Select, Textarea, Label, Fieldset, Table, Dialog, Details, Progress, Meter and the headings with no classes. A(..., cls='button') draws a link as a button.
A Div has no style. Give it cls='card', 'row', 'hstack', 'vstack' or 'container', or use a component function. The restyle layer also styles text, links, code, tables and focus rings.

title: fhoat
text:
Themes
The oat argument takes True, a preset name, a dict or a Theme. With oat=False, FastHTML uses Pico. fhoat puts the preset name on the <html> element as the data-theme attribute.

app, rt = fast_app(oat='blue')
test_eq(app.htmlkw['data_theme'], 'blue')
app.htmlkw

The presets are default zinc slate stone red rose orange amber yellow green teal blue indigo violet paper ink. paper and ink also change the page surfaces. Each preset has a light form and a dark form.
fast_app(oat=Theme(name='paper', primary=('#8a1f11', '#dcae6d'), radius='md', shadow='sm',
                   size='lg', font='serif', tokens=dict(container_max='64rem')))
radius, shadow and size set the default values. The user can change them with ThemePicker and FontToggle. ModeToggle changes the mode from auto to light to dark. The browser keeps the user’s choices in localStorage. It applies them before it shows the page.
Your JavaScript can make the same changes. For example, fhoat.set('radius', 'lg') sets a large radius, and fhoat.mode('dark') sets dark mode. fhoat.theme('teal') sets a preset. fhoat.cycle('size', ['', 'lg', 'xl']) sets the next value in the list. After each change, fhoat sends a fhoat event on <html>. The <html> element has the attributes data-mode, data-theme, data-radius, data-shadow and data-size. It also has the class dark or light.
fhoat puts its rules in Oat’s cascade layers. It puts the theme tokens in one :root rule outside the layers. Your CSS overrides fhoat without !important.

title: fhoat
text:
Layers
fast_app sends oat_kw to oat_hdrs. The flags in oat_kw select the layers.








flag
default
what it adds




presets
on
modes, presets and the user’s settings (themes.css)


components
on
card parts, grid, navbar, hero, footer and controls (components.css)


restyle
on
text, links, code, tables and focus rings (fhoat.css)


script
on
modes, settings, controls and toasts (fhoat.js, inline)


compat
off
Oat 1.0 tokens, metrics and titles, for an app made on Oat 1.0


cdn
off
Oat from jsDelivr, with SRI


prefix
/fhoat
the path of the files



The app serves the files at prefix. Each file URL has a hash of the file contents. The browser keeps each file in its cache for one year. fhoat loads nothing from a CDN unless you pass oat_kw=dict(cdn=True).
fast_app also takes mode, tips and store. mode sets the first mode: 'auto', 'light' or 'dark'. tips=False turns off Oat’s tooltips. store sets the name of the localStorage key.

title: fhoat
text:
An existing app
setup_oat adds Oat to an app that you already have. This includes an app that you made with FastHTML(...). After you call setup_oat_toasts, FastHTML’s add_toast(sess, msg, typ) shows Oat toasts.
app = FastHTML()
setup_oat(app, 'teal', restyle=False)
setup_oat_toasts(app)
To serve the files from a different path, mount OAT_DIR at that path and pass the path as prefix. To make the page head yourself, call oat_hdrs and oat_htmlkw.
app.router.routes.insert(0, Mount('/css/fhoat', StaticImmutable(directory=OAT_DIR)))
hdrs = oat_hdrs(restyle=False, presets=False, script=False, compat=True, prefix='/css/fhoat')

title: core
text:
Theme
A Theme is the app’s default look. name picks a preset from THEMES. radius, shadow and size become <html> attributes, so a reader’s choice in the browser replaces them. primary, font, display, scale and tokens become one unlayered :root rule, which beats the presets and Oat; your own unlayered CSS beats it.


source

Theme
def Theme(
    name:str=None, primary:str | tuple=None, radius:str=None, shadow:str=None, size:str=None, font:str=None,
    display:str=None, scale:float=None, tokens:dict=None
)->None:
The app’s default look: a preset name, an accent, corners, shadows, text size, type, scale and raw Oat tokens.



th = Theme(name='paper', primary=('#8a1f11', '#dcae6d'), radius='lg', font='serif', tokens=dict(container_max='60rem'), scale=1.1)
assert th.attrs() == dict(data_theme='paper', data_radius='lg')
assert '--primary:light-dark(#8a1f11, #dcae6d)' in th.css() and '--primary-foreground:light-dark(#fafafa, #0a0a0a)' in th.css()
assert '--container-max:60rem' in th.css() and 'font-size:110%' in th.css() and Theme().css() == ''
for bad in (dict(tokens=dict(x='red}</style><script>')), dict(tokens={'a;b': '1'}), dict(primary='red;x:y'), dict(radius='huge')):
    try: Theme(**bad); raise AssertionError(bad)
    except ValueError: pass
th.css()

title: core
text:
Headers
oat_hdrs gives the head tags; oat_htmlkw the <html> attrs that go with them. Each layer can be left out: an app with its own look passes restyle=False, an app with its own mode script presets=False, script=False, an app drawn on Oat 1.0 compat=True.


source

oat_htmlkw
def oat_htmlkw(
    theme:bool=True, mode:str='auto', tips:bool=True, store:NoneType=None
):
The <html> attrs fhoat.js reads: mode and look; tips=False hides Oat’s tooltips; store names the localStorage key.




source

oat_hdrs
def oat_hdrs(
    theme:bool=True, cdn:bool=False, prefix:str='/fhoat', compat:bool=False, presets:bool=True, components:bool=True,
    restyle:bool=True, script:bool=True
):
Head tags: Oat, then fhoat’s presets, components and restyle layers and its script; cdn takes Oat from jsDelivr (with SRI).



h = to_xml(oat_hdrs('blue', compat=True))
assert '/fhoat/oat.min.css?v=' in h and 'oat10.css' in h and 'oat10.js' in h and 'window.fhoat' in h and '=>' in h
h = to_xml(oat_hdrs(restyle=False, presets=False, components=False, script=False, prefix='/css/fhoat/'))
assert '/css/fhoat/oat.min.css?v=' in h and 'themes.css' not in h and 'fhoat.css' not in h and 'window.fhoat' not in h
assert 'integrity="sha384-' in to_xml(oat_hdrs(cdn=True)) and oatcss in to_xml(oat_hdrs(cdn=True))
assert oat_htmlkw(Theme(name='ink', size='lg'), tips=False, store='app') == dict(data_mode='auto', data_theme='ink', data_size='lg', data_tips='off', data_store='app')

title: core
text:
Serving and setup
serve_oat serves OAT_DIR ahead of FastHTML’s static catch-all, cached for a year (each URL carries a content hash). setup_oat does all of it on an existing app, the way setup_toasts does for FastHTML’s toasts: Oat’s headers go first in app.hdrs, its attrs into app.htmlkw (your own keys win), and the files get a route. It runs once per app.


source

setup_oat
def setup_oat(
    app, theme:bool=True, mode:str='auto', tips:bool=True, store:NoneType=None, **oat_kw
):
Put Oat and fhoat on an existing FastHTML app: headers, <html> attrs and the file route. oat_kw goes to oat_hdrs.




source

serve_oat
def serve_oat(
    app, prefix:str='/fhoat'
):
Serve fhoat’s files at prefix, ahead of fast_app’s static catch-all, cached for a year; once per prefix.




source

fast_app
def fast_app(
    *args, oat:bool=True, mode:str='auto', tips:bool=True, store:NoneType=None, oat_kw:NoneType=None,
    db_file:Optional[str]=None, render:Optional[<built-in function callable>]=None, hdrs:Optional[tuple]=None,
    ftrs:Optional[tuple]=None, tbls:Optional[dict]=None,
    before:Union[tuple, NoneType, fasthtml.core.Beforeware]=None, middleware:Optional[tuple]=None, live:bool=False,
    debug:bool=False, title:str='FastHTML page', routes:Optional[tuple]=None, exception_handlers:Optional[dict]=None,
    on_startup:Optional[<built-in function callable>]=None, on_shutdown:Optional[<built-in function callable>]=None,
    lifespan:Optional[<built-in function callable>]=None, default_hdrs:bool=True, surreal:Optional[bool]=True,
    htmx:Optional[bool]=True, htmx4:Optional[bool]=False, exts:Union[list, str, NoneType]=None, canonical:bool=True,
    secret_key:Optional[str]=None, key_fname:str='.sesskey', session_cookie:str='session_', max_age:int=31536000,
    sess_path:str='/', same_site:str='lax', sess_https_only:bool=False, sess_domain:Optional[str]=None,
    htmlkw:Optional[dict]=None, bodykw:Optional[dict]=None, reload_attempts:Optional[int]=1,
    reload_interval:Optional[int]=1000, static_path:str='.', body_wrap:<built-in function callable>=noop_body,
    nb_hdrs:bool=False, **kw
):
FastHTML’s fast_app with oat in place of pico: True, a preset name, a dict or a Theme; oat_kw goes to oat_hdrs.


One call gives an app with Oat, fhoat’s look and the reader’s mode and theme:

from starlette.testclient import TestClient
app, rt = fast_app(oat='blue')
@rt
def index(): return Titled('Hello', P('Oat'))
c = TestClient(app)
t = c.get('/').text
assert 'data-theme="blue"' in t and '/fhoat/oat.min.css?v=' in t and 'pico' not in t
assert t.index('oat.min.css') < t.index('htmx')
assert c.get('/fhoat/oat.min.js').headers['cache-control'].endswith('immutable') and c.get('/fhoat/core.py').status_code == 404
assert 'pico' in fast_app(oat=False)[0].hdrs.__repr__() and fast_app(pico=True)[0]

An existing app, or one built with FastHTML(...), takes setup_oat:

app = FastHTML()
setup_oat(app, 'teal', compat=True); setup_oat(app, 'teal')
assert len([r for r in app.router.routes if getattr(r, 'path', '') == '/fhoat/{fname}']) == 1 and app.htmlkw['data_theme'] == 'teal'
